summaryEn: A sixty-year-old glass maker flattened by China's property collapse — six straight quarters of losses, no dividend since 2021 — now being rescued by the least likely product in its catalogue: the low-dielectric glass cloth woven into the circuit boards of AI servers.
model: editorial (truth-audited: FinMind + press; glass framing — the Low DK fibreglass turn, +40–50% shipment guidance, NT$1.3bn new line and 38-million-metre capacity credited and placed upstream of Elite Material, but six consecutive loss quarters, four years of negative-to-zero EPS, no dividend since FY2021, and operating cash flow of essentially zero against NT$585m of net profit stated plainly; the 370× P/E is KEPT and explained because it is arithmetically correct and accurately signals near-zero earnings; sector 玻璃陶瓷 → Glass & Fiberglass)

sections.bodyMarkdown:
Taiwan Glass (台灣玻璃工業, TWSE: 1802) has made glass since **1964**. It **listed in July 1973**, built most of its capacity in mainland China, and spent the last several years being crushed there: Chinese property construction collapsed, flat-glass supply vastly exceeded demand, and Taiwan Glass posted **six consecutive loss-making quarters from 2024Q1 through 2025Q2**. Annual EPS across four years reads **−NT$0.25 (FY2022), +0.02 (FY2023), −0.55 (FY2024), −NT$0.20 (FY2025)**. It has **paid no dividend since FY2021**, when it distributed NT$1.82.

What is rescuing it is not glass for buildings. It is **glass cloth for circuit boards** — specifically **low-dielectric (Low DK) fibreglass fabric**, the woven reinforcement embedded inside copper-clad laminate, which is in turn the base material of every printed circuit board. As AI servers push signal speeds higher, the electrical properties of that glass cloth become a limiting factor, and the high-grade versions are in genuine shortage. This places Taiwan Glass **directly upstream of Elite Material (2383)**, also in this collection, whose high-speed laminates depend on exactly this fabric.

The turn is visible in the numbers. Gross margin has run **10.8% (2024Q4) → 13.7% (2025Q4) → 19.2% (2026Q1)**; operating margin from **−1.0% to +7.9%**; and 2026Q1 delivered **net profit of NT$585m and EPS of NT$0.20**. Monthly revenue has been growing **6–27%** year-on-year. Management guides **2026 high-end fibreglass cloth shipments up 40–50%**, and has committed **NT$1.3bn to a new specialty line** that takes **Low DK capacity to 38 million metres a year** when it starts in 2026. Industry expectations are that the Low DK shortage persists into the second half of 2027.

Two figures deserve to be read carefully rather than dismissed. The **P/E of 370×** is not a data error — trailing twelve-month EPS is **NT$0.13**, so the multiple is arithmetically correct, and it is retained on this page precisely because it tells the truth: **this company barely earns anything yet**. And **2026Q1 operating cash flow was essentially zero (−NT$1.66m) against NT$585m of reported net profit** — the recovery has not yet reached cash.

The honest read: **a traditional glass business still impaired by China, holding a genuinely scarce AI-materials asset it did not build for that purpose — early in a turn, priced at 2.82× book with no dividend and near-zero earnings.**

Taiwan Glass was founded in **1964**, when Taiwan needed windows. Flat glass is a foundational construction material, and making it requires a **float line** — a continuous furnace where molten glass floats across a bath of tin — that costs enormously, runs for years without stopping, and cannot be idled without damage. That capital structure defines the industry: **once you build a line, you must run it**, whatever the price of glass. The company **listed in 1973**.

Over the following decades it expanded into the adjacent products that share glass chemistry: **glass containers, and fibreglass** — molten glass drawn into filaments and woven into cloth. Fibreglass began as a reinforcement material for insulation and composites, an unglamorous industrial commodity.

The strategic decision that shaped the modern company was **China**. As mainland construction boomed, Taiwan Glass built the bulk of its capacity there, aligning itself with the largest construction market in history. For years that worked. Then Chinese property development collapsed, flat-glass demand fell with it, and an industry that cannot turn off its furnaces met an industry-wide surplus. The result was **six consecutive quarters of losses** and **four years without meaningful profit**.

The rescue came from the fibreglass division, and from a direction nobody planned for. **Woven glass cloth is the skeleton of every printed circuit board** — the fabric that copper-clad laminate is built around. As data rates in AI servers rose, the **dielectric properties of the glass itself** became a constraint: ordinary cloth distorts high-frequency signals. **Low-dielectric (Low DK) glass cloth** solves it, and very few producers can make it consistently. A commodity reinforcement material became a bottleneck component of the AI supply chain — and Taiwan Glass, sixty years into making windows, found itself holding one.

- **1964 (25 Aug)** — Taiwan Glass founded to make flat glass for Taiwan's construction industry.
- **1973 (20 July)** — **Lists on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (1802)**.
- **1970s–2000s** — Expands into glass containers and **fibreglass**; builds float lines and processing capacity.
- **2000s–2010s** — Concentrates major capacity expansion in **mainland China**, aligned with the construction boom.
- **2021** — Last dividend paid: **NT$1.82**. None since.
- **2022** — **FY2022 EPS −NT$0.25** as Chinese property weakens.
- **2023** — Break-even at best: **FY2023 EPS +NT$0.02**.
- **2024Q1–2025Q2** — **Six consecutive loss-making quarters.** FY2024 EPS **−NT$0.55**; FY2025 **−NT$0.20**.
- **2025Q3** — **Returns to profit**, ending the six-quarter run, as AI-driven demand lifts high-end fibreglass cloth.
- **2025Q4–2026Q1** — Recovery broadens: gross margin **13.7% → 19.2%**, operating margin **4.8% → 7.9%**; **2026Q1 net profit NT$585m, EPS NT$0.20**; monthly revenue up **6–27%** year-on-year.
- **2026** — **NT$1.3bn** committed to a new specialty fibreglass line taking **Low DK capacity to 38 million metres a year**; management guides **high-end fibreglass cloth shipments up 40–50%** for the year. Industry expects the Low DK shortage to persist into **H2 2027**.

Taiwan Glass's accounts show **a capital-heavy business emerging from a long impairment, with the recovery not yet in cash**.

- **Four years without earnings.** Annual EPS: **−NT$0.25 (FY2022), +0.02 (FY2023), −0.55 (FY2024), −NT$0.20 (FY2025)**, including **six consecutive loss-making quarters from 2024Q1 to 2025Q2**. Trailing **return on equity is 0.55%**.
- **A genuine margin turn.** Gross margin: **10.8% (2024Q4) → 10.9% → 10.0% → 11.7% → 13.7% (2025Q4) → 19.2% (2026Q1)**. Operating margin: **−1.0% → +7.9%** over the same period. Net profit reached **NT$585m in 2026Q1 (EPS NT$0.20)** — a single quarter exceeding any of the three preceding full years.
- **The P/E of 370× is correct, and is kept for that reason.** Trailing twelve-month EPS is **NT$0.13**, so at NT$48.15 the multiple genuinely is around 370×. It has not been removed from this page because it is not an error — it is an accurate statement that **the company's earnings are still close to nothing**, and hiding it would flatter the picture.
- **Cash has not followed profit.** **2026Q1 operating cash flow was −NT$1.66m** — essentially zero — against **NT$585m of net income**. For a recovering manufacturer rebuilding working capital this is explicable, but until operating cash flow turns convincingly positive the recovery is an accounting event more than an economic one.
- **A conservatively financed balance sheet.** **NT$91.6bn of assets** against **NT$52.5bn of equity** — a **42.7% debt ratio** — with **NT$7.5bn of cash**. This is the reason the company survived four bad years intact.
- **No dividend since FY2021.** Cash dividends (FinMind, by fiscal year): **NT$0.5 (2017) → 0.3 (2018) → 0.5 (2020) → NT$1.82 (2021)**, and nothing since. **Dividend yield is 0.00%** — accurately so.
- **Investing into the shortage.** **NT$1.3bn** for a new specialty fibreglass line lifting **Low DK capacity to 38 million metres a year**, against management guidance of **40–50% growth in high-end cloth shipments** in 2026.
- **Valuation.** **2.82× book** — a price that already reflects the AI-materials story rather than the earnings record.

The financing reality: **a survivor with a strong balance sheet and one genuinely valuable product line**, spending into a shortage while its ordinary business is still repairing.

**Stance: a loss-scarred traditional glass maker holding a scarce AI-materials asset — early in a real turn, but valued at 2.82x book on near-zero earnings, with no dividend and no cash generation yet.**

The bull case:

1. **A genuine bottleneck product.** **Low-dielectric (Low DK) glass cloth** is the woven reinforcement inside copper-clad laminate, and at AI-server data rates the glass itself limits signal integrity. Few producers make high-grade cloth consistently, and the shortage is expected to run **into the second half of 2027**. Taiwan Glass sits **upstream of Elite Material (2383)** in this collection's semiconductor chain.
2. **The turn is measurable, not narrative.** Gross margin **10.8% → 19.2%**, operating margin **−1.0% → +7.9%**, six consecutive loss quarters ended in 2025Q3, and **2026Q1 net profit of NT$585m** exceeded any of the prior three full years.
3. **Capacity being added into the shortage.** **NT$1.3bn** for a new line taking **Low DK capacity to 38 million metres a year**, with guidance of **40–50% growth** in high-end cloth shipments in 2026.
4. **A balance sheet that survived.** **42.7% debt ratio** and **NT$7.5bn of cash** — the reason the company is still here to participate.

The counter-arguments:

- **The base business is still impaired.** Most capacity serves **Chinese flat glass**, where property-driven oversupply has not resolved. High-end fibreglass is the smaller, better part of a company still dominated by the worse part.
- **Earnings are close to nothing.** **TTM EPS of NT$0.13** and **ROE of 0.55%**; the **370× P/E** is arithmetically real.
- **Cash has not arrived.** **Operating cash flow of essentially zero** against NT$585m of reported profit in 2026Q1.
- **No dividend since FY2021**, and none in prospect until earnings normalise.
- **Everyone is expanding into Low DK.** Shortages in materials end when capacity arrives, and Taiwan Glass is one of several producers building.

A **turnaround-with-an-option** thesis: a repaired balance sheet and a genuinely scarce product, bought before the earnings exist to justify the price.

Taiwan Glass melts sand into three quite different businesses:

- **Flat glass (the legacy core, and the problem).** Produced on **float lines** — continuous furnaces where molten glass floats across molten tin — for construction and automotive use. The economics are unforgiving: a float line costs enormously, **runs continuously for years, and cannot be idled without damaging it**. So when demand collapses, producers keep making glass and the price falls until someone shuts down permanently. Most of Taiwan Glass's capacity is in **mainland China**, where property construction fell sharply.
- **Glass containers.** Bottles and jars — a stable, regional, low-growth business.
- **Fibreglass, and specifically Low DK cloth (the reason to pay attention).** Molten glass drawn into filaments and woven into fabric. Ordinary fibreglass reinforces insulation and composites. But **electronic-grade glass cloth is the skeleton of every printed circuit board**: copper-clad laminate is built by impregnating this fabric with resin and facing it with copper foil. At AI-server data rates the **dielectric constant of the glass itself** distorts signals, so high-speed boards require **low-dielectric (Low DK) cloth** — which is difficult to produce consistently and currently scarce.
- **Where that sits in the chain.** Taiwan Glass's cloth feeds laminate makers such as **Elite Material (2383)**, whose laminate feeds substrate makers such as **Unimicron (3037)**, whose substrates carry the chips. Three companies in this collection, one supply chain, one AI demand signal.

The economics are **fixed-cost heavy with commodity pricing in the legacy business and shortage pricing in the new one**. That is why the margin move has been so sharp: gross margin rose from **10.8% to 19.2%** in five quarters, because a small high-value product line carries disproportionate profit against a mostly fixed cost base.

The strength is owning a scarce material inside an unglamorous company. The vulnerability is that **the scarce part is the minority of the business**, the majority is still Chinese flat glass, and float lines cannot be turned off while waiting.

Glass is two industries with the same raw material and opposite conditions.

- **Flat glass: structural oversupply centred on China.** China produces the majority of the world's flat glass, and its production was scaled for a property boom that ended. Because float lines cannot be economically idled, **surplus capacity keeps producing**, and prices stay depressed until lines are permanently closed. Chinese glass futures weakened through early 2025 on exactly this dynamic. Any producer with Chinese capacity — Taiwan Glass included — has been caught in it.
- **Electronic-grade fibreglass cloth: genuine shortage.** The opposite condition. **Low DK cloth** for high-speed PCBs requires specific glass formulations and weaving precision, and qualification into a laminate maker's product takes time. Demand is rising with AI server and high-speed networking build-out, and industry expectations are that **shortage persists into the second half of 2027**. Japan's **Nittobo** is the reference producer at the top of this market; Taiwanese and Chinese producers compete below it.
- **Why this matters more than the tonnage suggests.** Glass cloth is a small share of a circuit board's cost and an absolute constraint on its performance. That asymmetry — cheap input, non-substitutable function — is what creates pricing power, and it is the same asymmetry that makes Elite Material's high-speed laminates valuable one step downstream.
- **The competitive risk.** Material shortages are self-correcting. Taiwan Glass is adding **38 million metres a year of Low DK capacity**; so are its competitors. The current margin expansion reflects scarcity, and scarcity has a shelf life.

Taiwan Glass's position is **weak where it is large and strong where it is small**. The industry truth is that **a float-glass business tied to Chinese construction is a structurally poor place to be**, and that the fibreglass line is doing the work of justifying the whole company right now.

**Strengths**
- **Low DK fibreglass cloth** — a genuinely scarce AI-supply-chain material, upstream of Elite Material's high-speed laminates; industry shortage expected into **H2 2027**.
- **Sharp margin recovery**: gross **10.8% → 19.2%**, operating **−1.0% → +7.9%**; **2026Q1 net profit NT$585m** exceeded any of the three prior full years.
- **Balance sheet that survived four bad years**: **42.7% debt ratio**, **NT$7.5bn cash**, **NT$52.5bn equity**.
- **NT$1.3bn** new specialty line lifting Low DK capacity to **38 million metres a year**; guidance of **+40–50%** high-end cloth shipments.

**Weaknesses**
- **Six consecutive loss quarters (2024Q1–2025Q2)** and four years of negative-to-zero EPS.
- **TTM EPS NT$0.13, ROE 0.55%, P/E ~370×** — earnings are still nearly nothing.
- **Operating cash flow essentially zero** against NT$585m of 2026Q1 net profit.
- **No dividend since FY2021**; majority of capacity still in Chinese flat glass.

**Opportunities**
- AI and high-speed networking demand lifting Low DK volumes and prices.
- Mix shift toward electronic-grade cloth raising blended margin.
- Any stabilisation in Chinese construction relieving the legacy business.

**Threats**
- **Competitor Low DK capacity** arriving and ending the shortage.
- **Chinese flat-glass oversupply persisting**; float lines that cannot be idled.
- Energy and raw-material costs in an extremely fixed-cost process.

- **The company still barely earns anything.** **Trailing twelve-month EPS is NT$0.13** and **ROE is 0.55%**. The **370× P/E shown on this page is arithmetically correct**, not a data error, and it is retained deliberately: at **2.82× book**, the price reflects the AI-materials story, not the earnings.
- **Profit has not become cash.** **2026Q1 operating cash flow was −NT$1.66m** against **NT$585m of net profit**. Until those converge, the recovery is visible only in the income statement.
- **The majority of the business is still Chinese flat glass.** Property-driven oversupply has not resolved, and **float lines cannot be idled without damage**, so surplus capacity keeps producing. The high-margin fibreglass line is the smaller part of the company.
- **Material shortages end.** Taiwan Glass is adding **38 million metres a year** of Low DK capacity and competitors are doing the same. Today's **19.2% gross margin** reflects scarcity pricing; the historical pattern in materials is that capacity arrives and margins normalise.
- **Demand is derived from hyperscaler capital spending.** The Low DK cloth demand traces to AI server build-out — the same cycle driving Elite Material, Wiwynn and King Slide elsewhere in this collection. A pause there reaches Taiwan Glass through two intermediate layers.
- **No income while waiting.** **No dividend has been paid since FY2021**, and none is likely until earnings normalise. An investor is paid entirely in the hope of a re-rating.

Taiwan Glass's outlook turns on **whether high-end fibreglass grows fast enough to outrun the legacy glass business.** The axes to watch:

- **Gross margin.** The clearest single indicator, and currently the most encouraging: **10.8% (2024Q4) → 13.7% (2025Q4) → 19.2% (2026Q1)**. Continued expansion means the mix shift toward electronic-grade cloth is working; stalling means flat glass is still setting the company's economics.
- **Low DK shipments and the new line.** Guidance is **+40–50% in 2026**, with the **NT$1.3bn line** taking capacity to **38 million metres a year**. Whether that volume is absorbed at current prices determines the whole thesis.
- **Operating cash flow.** After **essentially zero in 2026Q1 against NT$585m of net profit**, this is the test of whether the recovery is economic. It is also the precondition for any dividend.
- **Chinese flat-glass conditions.** The larger half of the company. Stabilisation would turn a drag into a contributor; continued surplus caps the recovery regardless of how well fibreglass does.

Bottom line: Taiwan Glass is a **sixty-year-old glass maker whose ordinary business was flattened by China's property collapse — six straight loss quarters, four years of no earnings, no dividend since FY2021** — that happens to hold a **genuinely scarce AI-supply-chain material** in **low-dielectric glass cloth**, sitting upstream of Elite Material's high-speed laminates, with a shortage expected to run into **H2 2027** and **NT$1.3bn** committed to expanding it. The turn is real and measurable in the margin line; it is also **early, not yet in cash, and priced at 2.82× book on trailing EPS of NT$0.13**. Judge it on **gross margin and operating cash flow** — an option on AI materials attached to a business that has not yet recovered.
